CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ready to quit smoking.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presents with desire to quit smoking. Reports starting smoking in high school with experimental use progressing to regular daily use. Currently smokes approximately 1.5 packs per day with first cigarette within 1 hour of waking. Previously attempted smoking cessation using cold turkey method and successfully quit for almost a year but relapsed due to work-related stress from job layoffs and increased responsibilities. Currently highly motivated to quit due to impending fatherhood. Recently started meditation and joined a gym to manage stress. Considering nicotine patch as smoking cessation aid. Has selected next Monday (his birthday) as quit date.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Patient commended for taking first step toward smoking cessation. Will initiate 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Follow-up in 2 weeks to assess progress and reevaluate nicotine patch dosage.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be obtained at next visit for monitoring of glycemic control.

3. History of gout: Continue allopurinol. Advised to continue monitoring dietary triggers that may exacerbate uric acid levels.

Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks.
